findingDetails.title: Same-class inventory undercount: three more hub SKILL.md files still claim a hub ROUTER.md carries the release version (extends R1-P1-001)
findingDetails.case: A hub author or release operator in sk-code, system-deep-loop or cli-external-orchestration reads the hub SKILL.md version-authority paragraph, believes ROUTER.md carries the hub release version, and syncs or expects that parity; after any ROUTER.md body edit the pre-commit bump raises its own edition, the versions differ, and no gate reports it because this phase removed ROUTER.md from 13a.
findingDetails.evidence: Three live hub SKILL.md version-authority paragraphs at HEAD 95698b591b still list ROUTER.md as carrying the SKILL.md/release value: sk-code/SKILL.md:17 ('description.json, mode-registry.json, hub-router.json, ROUTER.md and README.md carry the same value'), system-deep-loop/SKILL.md:14 and cli-external-orchestration/SKILL.md:17 (same list without README.md). All contradict frontmatter-versioning.md:124 ('A hub ROUTER.md is not a release copy ... no gate compares it with SKILL.md') and the code at parent-skill-check.cjs:1850, whose follower list holds only the three JSON files. R1-P1-001 found the same class in three other sites (sk-doc/SKILL.md:17, sk-create-changelog/SKILL.md:261, examples-and-maintenance.md:181) but its scope proof covered only .skilled/commands and .skilled/skills/sk-doc, so these three hub files were never swept. The spec's in-scope bullet obliges the inventory over every live claim; tasks.md T002 is still unchecked. sk-code/SKILL.md:17 additionally lists README.md, a claim the retired 13c already contradicted, showing the paragraph is a shared hub template line left stale across hubs; the ROUTER.md clause is this phase's class.
findingDetails.userImpact: Hub authors keep writing and expecting ROUTER.md release parity; the changed behavior silently diverges from what their own hub documentation teaches, recreating the drift this phase exists to end.
findingDetails.scopeProof: rg -n 'ROUTER\.md' over .skilled/commands and .skilled/skills (md/yaml/json; excluding changelog, benchmark, reports, node_modules) filtered by version|release|carrier|bump|sync returned exactly three additional live claims (sk-code/SKILL.md:17, system-deep-loop/SKILL.md:14, cli-external-orchestration/SKILL.md:17) beyond the three sites R1-P1-001 recorded. The other hub candidates are clean: mcp-tooling/SKILL.md has no version-authority ROUTER.md line and sk-design/SKILL.md none; create-skill-parent-*.yaml and parent-skill-hub-template.md mention ROUTER.md only as a presence/four-part-format rule, which spec.md keeps out of scope; system-skill-advisor (T002's third directory) carries no version-parity claim.
findingDetails.recommendation: Complete T002 over the whole tree and correct the version-authority paragraph in all four hubs (sk-code, sk-doc, system-deep-loop, cli-external-orchestration) together with the two sk-doc instruction sites R1-P1-001 named: drop ROUTER.md from the release-copy list and state that it keeps its own edition; record each site in tasks.md/implementation-summary.md or correct it.
findingDetails.claim: The spec's same-class inventory is incomplete beyond the three sites R1-P1-001 recorded: three more live hub SKILL.md files still state that ROUTER.md carries the release version.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Checked whether the three lines are historical or generated (they are live SKILL.md files at HEAD); swept .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor, T002's third named directory (clean); swept every md/yaml/json under .skilled/commands and .skilled/skills for version-context ROUTER.md claims (only these three plus the R1-P1-001 sites); checked hub templates and create-skill YAML (presence/format only, consistent with own-edition).
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The builder may still intend to complete T002 before closure (it is unchecked), or may regard those hub SKILL.md paragraphs as outside the phase's file list. The spec's inventory bullet is not file-scoped and T002's grep is the declared mechanism, so the obligation covers them; if T002 later corrects or lists them, the finding downgrades per its trigger.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: If T002 completes and the three sites are corrected or listed with a reason in tasks.md/implementation-summary.md, or a follow-up commit corrects them, resolve or downgrade to P2; the class closes when every live claim agrees with frontmatter-versioning.md:124.
